stated: The Conservative Party will increase NHS spending above inflation every year, recruiting 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors by the end of the next Parliament, and driving up productivity through technology and moving care closer to homes via Pharmacy First, new GP surgeries, and Community Diagnostic Centres.

source.quote: Increase NHS spending above inflation every year, recruiting 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors, driving up productivity in the NHS and moving care closer to people’s homes through Pharmacy First, new and modernised GP surgeries and more Community Diagnostic Centres.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets NHS capacity, workforce, waiting times, and access to care — the core indicators of healthcare delivery.

A commitment to raise NHS spending above inflation every year across a full Parliament represents a large, compounding fiscal obligation; without identified revenue offsets, it materially shifts the funded-vs-borrowed balance and bears on debt-path sustainability.

membership_note: Policy bears on two fundamentals: its designed healthcare-access effect (O3) and the fiscal sustainability question raised by an open-ended above-inflation spending pledge (O12). Effects on O4 (no specific pay/conditions mechanism stated) and O14 (distributional access gain is real but secondary and not specified) are too diffuse or indirect to clear the non-negligible bar independently.
